items.definition: A green climbing plant that grows up walls and trees. It holds on tightly and hides what is behind it.
items.example: Ivy grew across the green door.

items.definition: An open space in the middle of woods, where the trees step back and the sky reaches the ground.
items.example: The path led to a small clearing.

items.definition: To put a seed into the ground and look after it. Planting is a promise to come back.
items.example: Bình planted the seed on the first of April.

items.definition: Kept out of sight, so that people walk past without noticing.
items.example: The door was hidden under the ivy.

items.definition: Something you want very much and keep safe. It can be gold, but it can also be a letter or a photograph.
items.example: The box in the grass held the real treasure.

items.definition: A drawing of a place, seen from above. A map shows you the way and shows you where things are.
items.example: Tuấn unfolded the old map on the kitchen table.

items.definition: A small hint. Clues come one after another, and each one points to the next.
items.example: The third clue was a picture of a bench and a nail.

items.definition: A small tool with a needle that points north. Explorers use a compass so they walk in a straight line.
items.example: The compass needle spun because of the iron in the ground.

items.definition: A small mountain, high in the middle and low at the edges. You can walk up a hill in a few minutes.
items.example: They walked up the hill to look for the treasure.

items.definition: A small sense organ on a robot. It tells the robot what is around it, or how it feels.
items.example: Bit's sensor flashed red when he was worried.

items.definition: The store of energy that makes a robot move. When it runs low, the robot has to plug in.
items.example: Bit's battery was getting low by the afternoon.

items.definition: A small switch you press to make something happen. Pressing a robot's button can wake it up.
items.example: He pressed the button on the old robot's chest.

items.definition: The place where a robot goes to fill its battery with energy.
items.example: Bit climbed down from the charging post.

items.definition: The room where a robot is built and repaired. It is full of tools and smells of metal and oil.
items.example: Bit found shiny silver paper in the workshop.

items.definition: A cover for your eyes with glass in it. It lets you see under the water clearly.
items.example: She pulled the diving mask down over her nose.

items.definition: Flat rubber shoes for your feet. They push the water behind you so you swim faster.
items.example: Her fins made a soft whirr in the water.

items.definition: A bottle of compressed air that a diver carries on their back and breathes from.
items.example: Her uncle checked the air tank before she jumped in.

items.definition: A hard, colourful structure built by tiny animals. It looks like a plant but it is alive, so never touch it.
items.example: The orange coral stood up like a tree.

items.definition: A whole underwater city of coral. Thousands of kinds of fish live there.
items.example: The reef was busy with small bright fish.

items.definition: The whole journey of an animal, from the egg all the way back to eggs again.
items.example: A butterfly's life cycle has four stages.

items.definition: The young stage of an insect. A butterfly larva is a caterpillar.
items.example: The larva eats and eats until it is fat.

items.definition: The resting stage, when the insect changes its body. A butterfly's pupa is a chrysalis.
items.example: Inside the pupa, the caterpillar becomes a butterfly.

items.definition: A big change of shape. A caterpillar turning into a butterfly is metamorphosis.
items.example: You can watch metamorphosis happen in a garden.

items.definition: The two thin feelers on an insect's head. They help it smell and feel its way.
items.example: The butterfly uses its antennae to find the flowers.

items.definition: The set of foods an animal eats. The diet can change with the season.
items.example: A bear's diet is berries, nuts and sometimes fish.

items.definition: An animal that eats both plants and animals, such as a bear, a pig or a person.
items.example: We are omnivores, so we eat rice and fish.

items.definition: A predator hunts and eats other animals. The animal being hunted is the prey.
items.example: The fox is the predator and the mouse is the prey.

items.definition: Animals that a farmer keeps on purpose, for food, for work or for company.
items.example: Cows, sheep and goats are all livestock on this farm.

items.definition: The big building on a farm where animals sleep and where the hay is kept.
items.example: The ponies sleep in the barn on cold nights.

items.definition: Eating grass that is growing out in a field.
items.example: The sheep are grazing in the long grass by the gate.

items.definition: Food given to farm animals, like hay, straw and roots.
items.example: We carry two buckets of fodder to the cows.

items.definition: An animal with six legs and a body in three parts: head, thorax and abdomen.
items.example: An ant is an insect because it has six legs.

items.definition: The hard outer shell of an insect. It protects the body but cannot stretch, so the insect must shed it to grow.
items.example: The empty shell of the cicada is left on the tree bark.

items.definition: The middle part of an insect's body. All six legs and the wings grow from it.
items.example: All six legs are attached to the thorax.

items.definition: The back part of an insect's body, where the stomach and the egg-making organs sit.
items.example: The wasp's abdomen is yellow and black.

items.definition: The one great body of salt water that covers most of the Earth.
items.example: The ocean is one big connected sea, not many small ones.

items.definition: A structure built by coral animals out of limestone, full of holes where small fish hide.
items.example: The coral reef grows a little slower every year.

items.definition: Tiny living things that drift with the currents near the surface of the sea.
items.example: The whale eats tonnes of plankton every day.

items.definition: A place where people buy or adopt animals and the things they need to live well.
items.example: We went to the pet shop to buy a food bowl.

items.definition: A person whose job is to treat sick animals and to help keep them healthy.
items.example: The vet says the puppy needs two more injections.
